mediawiki2005.title: MediaWiki, includes/OutputPage.php and includes/SquidUpdate.php as of commit 1833e43b5a03c75b3d18752b50fe6fbd83eea45e
mediawiki2005.author: MediaWiki contributors (file state; that commit itself is Antoine Musso, 'Move reporttime method from OutputPage object to a global function')
mediawiki2005.quote2:
# We'll purge the proxy cache for anons explicitly, but require end user agents
				# to revalidate against the proxy on each visit.
supports: the cacheability test is the presence of the PHP session cookie, not any per-page setting
an anonymous page is emitted with s-maxage for Squid; a logged-in page is emitted Cache-Control: private and the edge cannot serve it
the rule was already in the source in September 2005, the year the Amsterdam cache cluster started
the op-code Wikimedia actually sent is HTCP CLR: SquidUpdate::HTCPPurge in the same 2005 revision sets $htcpOpCLR = 4 and socket_sendto()s the packet to $wgHTCPMulticastAddress

rfc2756.title: Hyper Text Caching Protocol (HTCP/0.0)
rfc2756.author: P. Vixie (ISC), D. Wessels (NLANR)
rfc2756.venue: Network Working Group, Request for Comments: 2756, Experimental
rfc2756.quote: Tell a cache to completely forget about an entity. RD is honoured.
rfc2756.quote2: This document describes HTCP, a protocol for discovering HTTP caches and cached data, managing sets of HTTP caches, and monitoring cache activity. This is an experimental protocol, one among several proposals to perform these functions.
rfc2756.quote3: Clearing a URI without specifying response, entity, or cache headers means to clear all entities using that URI.
supports: HTCP is a real, published protocol whose CLR op-code is an explicit cache-invalidation instruction
the wording 'completely forget about an entity' is the RFC's own description of CLR

bergsma2007.title: Wikimedia architecture
bergsma2007.author: Mark Bergsma, Wikimedia Foundation Inc.
bergsma2007.pages: 32-slide deck, read in full via pdftotext -layout
bergsma2007.quote: Hit rates: 85% for Text, 98% for Media, since the use of CARP
bergsma2007.quote2: If a MediaWiki feature is too expensive, it doesn’t get enabled on Wikipedia
bergsma2007.quote4: 350 servers, ranging between 1x P4 to 2x Xeon Quad-Core, 0.5 - 16 GB of memory
bergsma2007.quote6: Yearly budget of around $2M, supported mostly through donations
bergsma2007.quote7: Currently has 9 employees, the rest is done by volunteers
bergsma2007.quote10: Secondary caching-only clusters in Amsterdam, the Netherlands and Seoul, South Korea
bergsma2007.quote11: HTTP reverse proxy caching implemented using Squid
bergsma2007.quote12: Split into two groups with different characteristics
bergsma2007.quote13: ‘Text’ for wiki content (mostly compressed HTML pages)
bergsma2007.quote14: ‘Media’ for images and other forms of relatively large static files
bergsma2007.quote15: Invalidation through expiry times not acceptable, explicit cache purging needs to be done
bergsma2007.quote16: Only the latest revision of a page should be served at all times in order not to hinder collaboration
bergsma2007.quote17: Implemented using the UDP based HTCP protocol: on edit application servers send out a single message containing the URL to be invalidated, which is delivered over multicast to all subscribed Squid caches
bergsma2007.quote18: 1 Image server containing 1.3 TB of data, 4 million files
bergsma2007.quote21: 10th busiest site in the world (source: Alexa)
bergsma2007.quote22: 55 Squid servers currently, plus 20 waiting for setup
bergsma2007.quote23: New file / directory layout structure, using content hashes for file names
bergsma2007.quote24: Files with the same name/URL will have the same content, no invalidation necessary
supports: the 85% text / 98% media edge hit rates
Tampa as the only application cluster; Amsterdam and Seoul as caching-only
purge on edit is multicast HTCP, not TTL expiry
the scale and the money: 30 000 req/s peak, 350 servers, ~6 operators, ~$2M/year, 9 employees
the media origin was one overloaded image server
the product rule that a MediaWiki feature too expensive to serve does not get enabled
bergsma2007.note_on_glyphs: Quotes are as pdftotext -layout renders the PDF, including the deck's typographic apostrophes and single quotes. The story reproduces quote2 with a straight apostrophe.

wikitech_esams.title: Esams data center — Wikitech (the year given is the founding year the page documents, not a publication year; the page is a living document retrieved 2026-08-22)
wikitech_esams.author: Wikimedia Foundation / Wikitech contributors
wikitech_esams.quote: This data center started around 2005 under the name '''knams''' ("kn" from [[w:Kennisnet|Kennisnet]], the operator at the time, and "AMS" from the code for [[w:Amsterdam_Airport_Schiphol|Amsterdam Schiphol Airport]]).
wikitech_esams.quote2: '''esams''' (pronounced ''ee-sams'') is a caching data center located at [[w:Digital_Realty|Digital Realty's]] AMS9 data center
wikitech_esams.quote3: In 2008, most of the equipment was moved to the EvoSwitch AMS-1 data center.
wikitech_esams.quote4: In 2023, everything was consolidated in knams, which was renamed esams to minimize the need for code changes.
supports: the Amsterdam caching cluster started around 2005, under the name knams
Amsterdam is still a caching data center for Wikimedia today

wikitech_coof.title: Caching servers out of Florida — Wikitech (contemporaneous write-up of the Paris squid experiment; first revision on Wikitech 2005-01-12, 'moved from meta'; now at Obsolete:Caching servers out of Florida)
wikitech_coof.author: David Monniaux and Wikitech contributors
wikitech_coof.quote: A network round-trip (measured using ping) from a French network node to the Paris squids takes 4-5 ms, about 25-35 ms from a DSL client with basic settings (some DSL lines will go faster); compare this to 110 ms (and sometimes 150 ms) to the Florida cluster from a French network node (140 ms from a DSL client).
wikitech_coof.quote2: The machines were put in active usage on Sunday, January 9, 2005.
wikitech_coof.quote3: Previously, all content was served exclusively out of servers based in Florida.
wikitech_coof.quote4: The machines exclusively provide Squid service.
wikitech_coof.quote5: According to [http://bleuenn.wikimedia.org:8080/country-stats statistics], we have an about 75%-80% hit rate, climbing to 95% for multimedia content.
supports: the distance number the story uses: 110 ms from a French network node to Florida against 4-5 ms to squids near Paris
Wikimedia was already running an edge cache in Europe (Lost Oasis racks near Paris) from 9 January 2005, before the Amsterdam site started
the rationale for caching outside Florida is latency plus donated bandwidth, stated by Wikimedia at the time

unverified: The exact date and venue of Mark Bergsma's 'Wikimedia architecture' deck. No slide carries a date; the PDF is an Apple Keynote 3.0.2 re-export whose CreationDate is 2009-04-20/21, and its Wikitech file page carries no description text (the upload record reads 'recovered file, missing upload log entry', 2009-04-20). The 2007 in the filename is corroborated only by the deck's own content — ~$2M yearly budget, 9 employees, 8 million articles, 110 million revisions, 10th busiest site per Alexa — all of which fit 2007 and not 2008+. No sentence in the story dates the deck or any figure from it; cards c1 and c4 do carry 2007, on that content evidence alone.

Seoul was NOT a caching-only site in the story's 2005 frame, so the story no longer mentions it. Wikitech dates yaseo to September 2005 (wikitech-l, September 2005; Server admin log, 9 September 2005) — after the first Amsterdam rack page (31 May 2005) — and lists its usage as 'Core services (zhwiki, kowiki)'. The Yaseo migration plan records ko/ja/ms/th wikis, uploads and MySQL masters being moved from yaseo to pmtpa on 29 September 2006. The 2007 deck's 'secondary caching-only clusters in Amsterdam ... and Seoul' is true of 2007, not of 2005.

The claim in the allocation brief that the logged-in minority consumes almost all application and database capacity. The 2005 source code confirms logged-in readers bypass the edge entirely; no source I could open quantifies their share of load, so no share is stated.

The claim in the allocation brief that one edit to a widely transcluded template fires a purge across millions of pages and that the job queue backlog, not delivery, was the real ceiling. Not confirmed from any source opened here, and absent from the prose.

Domas Mituzas's 2007 MySQL Conference tutorial 'Wikipedia: Site internals, configuration, code examples and management issues'. The copy at dom.as/uc/workbook.pdf returned HTTP 403. He is not named in the story.

Whether Wikimedia leased the Amsterdam racks from Kennisnet in 2005 specifically. Wikitech names Kennisnet only as 'the operator at the time' and gives no lease date, so Kennisnet is not named in the story.

Paris WAS a Wikimedia edge cache, and earlier than Amsterdam: the Lopar cluster in Lost Oasis racks at the Telecity colocation in Aubervilliers went into active use on 9 January 2005 (three donated Celeron boxes, Squid only), and Wikitech's Data centers page lists it as Paris, France / Edge caching / 2005. The 2007 deck's silence about Paris does not rule it out — the cluster was gone by then. The story now uses its latency numbers and no longer claims that every European page view crossed the Atlantic.

Whether the Amsterdam racks held Squids and nothing else. The first Kennisnet rack plan (Wikitech, 31 May 2005) lists nine Sun V20z, a management V40z and a 'Database (Sun V40z)', and the site later also housed Wikimedia Deutschland's Toolserver hardware. 'Caching-only' in the deck describes the production serving path — no MediaWiki application servers — which is all the story claims.
